con.aces.a1: This site was built to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA: minimum contrast of 4.5:1, full keyboard navigation, always-visible focus, alternative text on every image and forms with associated labels.
con.aces.a2: If you find a barrier to access, report it to [[MAIN_EMAIL]]. The council undertakes to reply within ten working days and to state the timeframe for correction.

con.cookies.a1: This site uses no tracking cookies and no advertising. It stores only three things in your browser: the language you chose, your high-contrast preference and your conversation history with the assistant.
con.cookies.a2: This data stays on your device and can be deleted at any time, by clearing site data in your browser or using the clear conversation button in the assistant window.

mun.geo.p1: The island is mostly flat, with gentle relief rising inland and peaking at Monte Penoso. The absence of high mountains explains the scarce rainfall: Maio is one of the driest municipalities in Cabo Verde and depends on desalination and groundwater for public supply.
mun.geo.p2: The north-easterly wind blows almost all year. It shapes the dunes of Morrinho, drives evaporation in the salt pans and is increasingly studied as an energy resource for the municipality.
mun.geo.p3: The dominant vegetation is American acacia, planted in afforestation campaigns and today concentrated in the protected area of Barreiro and Figueira — the largest continuous woodland in the archipelago.
mun.geo.tabela: Territory at a glance — figures to be confirmed by council services
mun.geo.title: Plateau, dunes and constant wind
mun.hist.p1: Permanent settlement of Maio began with salt. Through the 17th and 18th centuries, English and North American ships anchored off Porto Inglês to load salt gathered from the natural pans — hence the name the town became known by. Salt paid taxes, fed families and drew the coastline still visible in plan today.
mun.hist.p2: Goat herding and artisanal fishing settled people inland and along the north coast. The localities grew around wells, pens and sheltered landings rather than an urban plan: that is why the municipality has twelve settlements, each with its own identity.
mun.hist.p3: The municipality of Maio was created with the administrative division of the archipelago and has kept a single district ever since, coinciding with the whole island. Today the council serves close to [[POPULATION]] residents.
mun.hist.quote: “Anyone arriving in Maio by sea sees the salt pans first. It is the oldest drawing the island has of itself.”
mun.hist.title: From salt to municipality
mun.lede: Maio is the easternmost municipality of the Leeward group. It has a single seat — Vila do Maio, also called Porto Inglês — and twelve localities spread across a plateau that rarely rises above four hundred metres.
mun.loc.alcatraz: Small settlement between the plateau and the east coast.
mun.loc.calheta: Artisanal fishing harbour and sheltered beach.
mun.loc.figueira: Gateway to the Barreiro protected area.
mun.loc.lede: The council runs decentralised front-desk service and waste collection in all of them. Service dates in each locality are published at the start of every month.
mun.loc.morro: Largest settlement in the north, monthly fair and secondary school.
mun.loc.pilao: Farming settlement in the centre of the island.
mun.loc.santoantonio: Exposed coast, fishing and an annual pilgrimage.
mun.loc.title: The twelve localities
mun.loc.vila: Porto Inglês. Town Hall, port, airfield and salt pans.

serv.agua.p1: Municipal Water Services supply the network from the desalination unit and the municipality's boreholes. Meters are read monthly and billing follows the consumption bands approved by the Municipal Assembly.
serv.agua.p2: Report it immediately by phone to the Citizen Desk. Outside opening hours, use the emergency number posted at the Town Hall. Bursts on the public road take priority over any other request.
serv.agua.resposta: The water bill is paid at the council treasury in Vila do Maio by the 20th of each month; late payment incurs interest and can lead to supply being cut off.
serv.agua.title: Water and sanitation

serv.aside.title: Can't find your case?
serv.aside2.title: In-person service
serv.cem.p1: The municipality has cemeteries in Vila do Maio, Morro and Calheta. Applications for perpetual grave concessions, transfers and exhumations are made in writing and decided within ten working days.
serv.cem.resposta: Burial is authorised at the Citizen Desk on presentation of the death certificate, on any working day and, in urgent cases, at weekends too.
serv.cem.title: Municipal cemeteries
serv.cert.l1: Valid identification document of the applicant.
serv.cert.l2: Power of attorney, when a third party applies.
serv.cert.l3: Exact statement of the purpose of the certificate.
serv.cert.l4: Proof of payment of the applicable fee.
serv.cert.p1: The council issues certificates of residence, municipal property, business activity, boundaries and the content of decisions. People living off the island can apply by email, attaching a copy of their identification document; a scanned certificate is sent back and the original is held for collection.
serv.cert.p3: Certificate requiring an archive search: 10 working days.
serv.cert.p4: Urgent request: subject to the higher fee set in the municipal schedule.
serv.cert.resposta: To request a certificate, bring your identification document and proof of payment of the fee to the Citizen Desk; the certificate is ready within five working days.
serv.cert.title: Certificates and declarations
serv.faq.a1: You need a valid identification document and proof of payment of the fee. If someone else applies on your behalf, a signed power of attorney is required. The certificate is ready within five working days at the Citizen Desk.
serv.faq.a2: The Citizen Desk is open Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 15:30, without a break. The treasury closes at 14:30. Services are closed on municipal and national public holidays.
serv.faq.a3: Pay at the council treasury by the 20th of each month, with the bill or your contract number. Late payment incurs interest and, after two months in arrears, supply is suspended until the account is settled.
serv.faq.a4: Yes. Certificates, proofs and duplicates can be requested by email, with a copy of your identification document and a statement of purpose. The council replies within five working days and sends the scanned document; the original is held for collection by you or by a representative.
serv.faq.a5: Maintenance work — painting, replacing roof tiles, repairing plumbing — needs only prior written notification. Any change to area, facade or structure requires a building permit with a project signed by a qualified professional.
serv.faq.a6: The budget, the activity plan and the annual accounts are on the Transparency page, in PDF and filterable by year. Documents from before 2015 are consulted in person at the municipal archive.

serv.faq.q2: What are the opening hours of Maio Municipality Council?

serv.lede: Every service on this page states three things first: which documents to bring, how long it takes and where it is done. If anything is missing, ask Nha Câmara or call the Citizen Desk.

serv.lic.l2: Identification document and tax identification number.

serv.lic.p1: The municipal licence covers shops, restaurants, bars and local accommodation, as well as terraces, outdoor advertising and use of public space. Food and drink establishments also need an opinion from the health office.
serv.lic.resposta: To open an establishment in the municipality, submit the commercial licence application at the Citizen Desk before starting to trade; the decision is communicated within fifteen working days.
serv.lic.title: Commercial licensing
serv.merc.p1: The Municipal Market of Vila do Maio opens Monday to Saturday, 06:00 to 14:00. The Morro fair is held on the third Sunday of each month and the Calheta fair on the first Saturday. Stalls are allocated by annual draw, with priority for producers from the municipality.
serv.merc.resposta: To sell in the municipal market you need a seller's card issued by the council, renewed each January.
serv.merc.title: Markets and fairs
serv.res.caption: Collection calendar by locality
serv.res.nota: Construction rubble, furniture and appliances are not collected with household waste. Book removal at the Citizen Desk.
serv.res.resposta: Household waste is collected in the late afternoon, on the days set for each locality; put closed bags in the nearest container after 18:00.
serv.res.title: Waste and street cleaning
serv.tax.caption: Most requested fees — amounts to be confirmed by council services
serv.tax.resposta: The amounts in force are set out in the Fees and Licences Regulation approved by the Municipal Assembly; check the document before paying.
serv.tax.title: Fees and licences

serv.urb.e2: Submission of the architectural project signed by a qualified professional.

serv.urb.p1: The application goes to the Planning Division, which checks compliance with the municipal master plan, issues the alignment and schedules the inspection. Starting work without a permit exposes the owner to a stop notice and a fine.
serv.urb.resposta: Building, extending or altering the facade of a building in the municipality requires a building permit applied for before works start; simple maintenance work needs only prior notification.

tur.chegar.p1: By sea, the ferry links Praia (Santiago) to Vila do Maio in a crossing of about three hours. By air, there are regular flights to Maio Airfield from Praia. Always confirm times the day before: they depend on the sea and the wind.
tur.chegar.p2: On the island, shared taxis (“hiace”) run between Vila and the localities, most frequently in the morning. Renting a car is advisable for the northern beaches.
tur.chegar.title: Getting here
tur.ficar.cta: Request the list of licensed accommodation
tur.ficar.p1: The municipality has small hotels, guesthouses and local accommodation, concentrated in Vila do Maio and Calheta. Every establishment must be licensed by the council: ask for the licence number before booking.
tur.ficar.p2: The up-to-date list of licensed accommodation is provided by the Citizen Desk.
tur.ficar.title: Where to stay
tur.lede: Thirty kilometres of near-deserted beach, the largest acacia woodland in the archipelago, turtles nesting from June to October, and a goat cheese found nowhere else.
tur.nat.p1: The Barreiro and Figueira Nature Reserve protects the largest continuous acacia woodland in Cabo Verde. It is a place of rare shade on a dry island, and the best spot in the archipelago to watch migratory birds at dawn.
tur.nat.p2: The Porto Inglês salt pans are still worked by hand. The basins change colour with the stage of evaporation — from green to pink — and in the late afternoon the salt crust reflects the light like a broken mirror.
tur.nat.p3: The interior is goat country, with dry stone pens. The trails between Pilão Cão and Cascabulho take two hours on foot, always with the wind behind you.
tur.nat.r1: Do not drive off the marked tracks.
tur.nat.r2: Do not collect salt, plants or shells in protected areas.
tur.nat.r3: Take your rubbish with you: there is no collection outside the localities.
tur.nat.title: Acacias, salt pans and birds
tur.praia1.desc: Ten minutes' walk from Vila. Fine sand, shallow water and a beach bar open all year.
tur.praia2.desc: Kilometres without a patch of shade and almost without a soul. Bring water and a hat.
tur.praia3.desc: A fishermen's beach. The catch lands late in the morning and is sold right there.
tur.praias.lede: The south and east coasts have white sand and calm water; in the north the wind raises a swell and swimming demands care.
tur.praias.title: The beaches
tur.sab.d1: Made in the morning, eaten the same day, with cane honey.
tur.sab.d2: Fish from artisanal boats, served the day it lands.
tur.sab.d3: The everyday dish. At breakfast, fried up again.
tur.sab.d4: Gathered by hand in the Porto Inglês basins.
tur.sab.n4: Fleur de sel from the pans
tur.sab.title: What people eat in Maio
tur.tartarugas.texto: Loggerhead turtles nest on Maio's beaches between June and October. Watching nests is allowed only with accredited guides. Never use white light or flash: it disorients females and hatchlings.
tur.tartarugas.title: Turtles: June to October
tur.title: The island that is in no hurry
